question.problem: Given that $f(x,y)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{y-{x}^{2}}},$ find the set of values $(x,y)$ on which $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ exists.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $f(x,y)$ is defined only when 

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{x}^{2} & >0 \\ y & >{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of $f$ is 

$$
{D}_{f}=\{(x,y)\,:\,y>{x}^{2}\}.
$$

Now, we compute the partial derivative of $f(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{y-{x}^{2}}}) \\  & =-\frac{-2x}{2(y-{x}^{2})^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{x}{(y-{x}^{2})^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

The function ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ is defined only for 

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{x}^{2} & >0 \\ y & >{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of ${f}_{x}$ is

$$
{D}_{{f}_{x}}=\{(x,y)\,:\,y>{x}^{2}\}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ exists on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{x}} & =\{(x,y)\,:\,y>{x}^{2}\}\cap \{(x,y)\,:\,y>{x}^{2}\} \\  & =\{(x,y)\,:\,y>{x}^{2}\}.\end{aligned}
$$
